headline_marked: Photon raises [[$4.5M seed funding]] to build AI agents over messaging apps
headline: Photon raises $4.5M seed funding to build AI agents over messaging apps
summary: The AI startup held a 'funeral' for mobile apps and is now backed by investors including Vercel to develop its agent-building tools.
details: Photon, an AI startup focused on building agents that operate within existing messaging apps like iMessage and WhatsApp, has secured $4.5 million in seed funding. The company aims to replace the traditional mobile app model with AI-powered agents accessible through familiar communication platforms.

The funding round was co-led by Gradient and A*, with participation from Vercel, HongShan, Z Fellows, Llama Ventures, and Karman. This investment will fuel Photon's development of its tools, which include a unified API, an extensible channel framework, a CLI, and an observability suite.

Photon's co-founder and CEO Daniel Tian famously held a 'funeral' for mobile apps to highlight the company's vision. He believes the era of installing new apps is ending, with users preferring to interact with agents through apps they already use daily.

The startup's open-source version has gained significant traction, with over 40,000 developer sign-ups. Photon also offers a managed platform with 99.95% uptime and compliance certifications like SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA, catering to enterprise needs.

Photon's technology is already being used by companies such as Corgi Insurance, Ditto, and Rho. Integration partners include Vercel and Nous Research, with its technology powering layers for Tencent's QClaw and NanoClaw.

The company reported a 10x revenue growth in just four months and a churn rate of less than 3%. Messaging volume has also seen a 5x increase in the last month alone, indicating strong adoption and engagement.

topic: deepseek and huawei release open-source ai programming tools
headline_marked: [[DeepSeek & Huawei]] release open-source tools for Ascend AI chips
headline: DeepSeek & Huawei release open-source tools for Ascend AI chips
summary: New programming tools aim to simplify development and reduce reliance on Nvidia's ecosystem for AI computation and chip-to-chip communication.
details: Chinese AI firm DeepSeek, in partnership with Huawei, has launched open-source programming tools for Huawei's Ascend AI chips. This move is part of a broader strategy to decrease dependence on Nvidia's dominant hardware and software ecosystem.

The new toolkit includes libraries for AI computation and chip-to-chip communication, alongside Ascend support for the high-level programming language TileLang. Huawei provided full development support, aiming to simplify programming and maximize hardware performance.

Key components include DeepGEMM-Ascend for matrix multiplication and calculations, supporting BF16, FP8, and FP4 operations with familiar APIs for developers. DeepEP-Ascend manages communication for training and inference, crucial for large AI models.

TileLang offers a higher-level programming layer, described as having a simpler model than Nvidia's CUDA, to boost development efficiency. While it supports multiple platforms, including Nvidia GPUs, the update adds native support for Ascend 950.

These tools are built upon Huawei's CANN software platform. The release aims to challenge Nvidia's long-standing advantage in the AI computing market, which is largely attributed to its mature CUDA programming environment and optimized libraries.

This collaboration follows Huawei's recent unveiling of its next-generation AI processors and supernode systems, with expectations for widespread AI system adoption for model training by 2027. DeepSeek's V4 model previously saw collaboration with Huawei's Ascend chips.
